answer: A stake-bonded reputation ledger makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, like a juniper sapling that only grows if it survives the season. A single bad act slashes the bond and pushes the agent off the ledge of trust, so an attacker must fund each fake identity separately — no velvet shortcut lets one deposit cover a thousand sock puppets. Honest agents earn their bond back with interest.
